Introduction

Technology can make everyday life safer, easier and more independent. Our Smart Blind Stick project is a school science project designed to demonstrate how sensors, microcontrollers, audio feedback, GPS and GSM communication can be combined to support people with visual impairment.

Traditional blind sticks help users identify obstacles through physical contact. Our prototype extends that basic concept by using electronic sensing and communication features. The project is divided into System 01 and System 02, allowing the different functions to be developed and demonstrated clearly.

01 • What is a Blind Stick?

A blind stick is a mobility aid that helps people with visual impairment move around by detecting or physically contacting obstacles. A Smart Blind Stick adds electronic sensors and feedback to this basic idea.

Our prototype uses Arduino-based electronics to collect information from sensors and provide useful outputs. The design is divided into two systems so each function can be developed and tested separately.

02 • How can it help people?

  • Helps detect nearby obstacles using ultrasonic sensors.
  • Can provide audio information through a speaker.
  • Can sense light and moisture as environmental inputs.
  • Can obtain location information through GPS.
  • Can provide cellular communication through GSM.
  • Shows how embedded electronics can be applied to an accessibility-focused prototype.

Note: This is a school science prototype and is not a certified medical or safety device.

03 • Features of Our Smart Blind Stick

🔊 Audio feedback

DFPlayer Mini + microSD + mini speaker can deliver stored audio/voice messages.

📡 Multi-sensor detection

Three ultrasonic sensors are included in System 01 for distance/obstacle sensing.

💡 LDR sensing

Light-level information is included as an environmental input.

💧 Moisture sensing

A soil-moisture sensor is included for an additional environmental input.

📍 GPS

NEO-6M is included for location information.

📶 GSM

SIM800L is included for cellular communication.
